quals-wisconsin-algebra-1998s-01.prompt:
Fix a prime $p$ and let $G$ be a finite group with the property that every nonidentity $p$-subgroup of $G$ is contained in a unique Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$. Suppose $N\trianglelefteq G$ and $|N|$ is divisible by $p$.

(i) If $P$ and $Q$ are Sylow $p$-subgroups of $G$, show that $Q=P^n$ for some element $n\in N$.

(ii) Prove that $G/N$ has a unique Sylow $p$-subgroup.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1998s-01.answer: (i) $P\cap N,\,Q\cap N\in\mathrm{Syl}_p(N)$, so $Q\cap N=(P\cap N)^n$ with $n\in N$; the nonidentity $p$-group $Q\cap N$ lies in both $Q$ and $P^n$, so $Q=P^n$. (ii) Sylow subgroups of $G/N$ are images $PN/N$, and $P^nN/N=PN/N$.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1998s-02.prompt:
Let $R$ be a commutative domain and write $(a)$ for the principal ideal generated by $a\in R$. Recall that an element of $R$ is said to be irreducible if it is nonzero, not a unit, and has no proper factorization.

(i) Show that $(a)\subseteq(b)$ if and only if $b\mid a$, and that $(a)=(b)$ if and only if $b=au$ for some unit $u\in R$.

(ii) If $R$ is a UFD (unique factorization domain), prove that the set of principal ideals of $R$ satisfies the maximal condition.

(iii) If the set of principal ideals of $R$ satisfies the maximal condition, show that every nonzero, nonunit element of $R$ can be written as a finite product of irreducible elements.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1998s-02.answer: (i) $(a)\subseteq(b)\iff a\in(b)$; mutual divisibility plus cancellation gives a unit. (ii) Choose $(a)$ in the family with the fewest prime factors; a strictly larger $(b)$ would have $b$ a proper divisor with fewer prime factors. (iii) A maximal counterexample $(a)$ factors as $bc$ with $(b),(c)\supsetneq(a)$, which are products of irreducibles.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1998s-03.prompt:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $F\subseteq K$ be fields of characteristic $0$, and assume that $F$ contains a primitive $p$th root of unity. Fix $a\in K$.

(i) Prove that there exists a field $E\supseteq K$ such that $E$ contains a $p$th root of $a$ and $|E:K|=1$ or $p$.

(ii) Now assume that $K$ is a finite degree Galois extension of $F$. Show that there exists a field $E\supseteq K$ such that $E$ contains a $p$th root of $a$, $E$ is Galois over $F$, and $|E:K|$ is a power of $p$.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1998s-03.answer: (i) Let $E$ be the splitting field of $x^p-a$ over $K$; any one root generates it (roots differ by $p$th roots of unity in $F$), so all irreducible factors have degree $|E:K|$, which divides $p$. (ii) Adjoin to $K$ the roots of $\prod_{\sigma\in\mathrm{Gal}(K/F)}(x^p-\sigma(a))\in F[x]$ one factor at a time; $E$ is a splitting field over $F$, and each step has degree $1$ or $p$ by (i).

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1998s-04.prompt:
Let $V$ be a finite dimensional vector space over a field of characteristic $0$. Suppose $T\colon V\to V$ is a linear operator such that the trace $\mathrm{tr}\,T^k=0$ for all integers $k\ge1$.

(i) Show that the constant term of the characteristic polynomial of $T$ is zero, and deduce that $T(V)\neq V$.

(ii) Let $S$ denote the restriction of $T$ to the subspace $T(V)$, so that $S$ is a linear operator on $T(V)$. Prove that $\mathrm{tr}\,S^k=0$ for all integers $k\ge1$.

(iii) Show that $T$ is nilpotent.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1998s-04.answer: (i) Take the trace of Cayley–Hamilton $T^n+a_1T^{n-1}+\cdots+a_nI=0$: $na_n=0$, so $a_n=0$, $\det T=0$. (ii) In a basis extending one of $T(V)$, $T=\begin{pmatrix}A&*\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, so $\mathrm{tr}\,S^k=\mathrm{tr}\,A^k=\mathrm{tr}\,T^k$. (iii) Induction on $\dim V$: $S$ is nilpotent, so $T^{j+1}=S^jT=0$.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1998s-05.prompt:
Let $G$ be a (not necessarily finite) group and let $\theta\colon G\to G$ be a homomorphism such that $\theta^n(G)=\{1\}$ for some integer $n\ge1$.

(i) If the kernel of $\theta$ is finite, prove that the kernel of $\theta^2$ is finite, and deduce that $G$ is finite.

(ii) If $\theta(G)$ has finite index in $G$, prove that $\theta^2(G)$ has finite index in $G$, and deduce that $G$ is finite.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1998s-05.answer: (i) $\theta$ maps $H=\ker\theta^2$ into $\ker\theta$ with kernel $\ker\theta$, so $|H|\le|\ker\theta|^2$; then induct on $n$ using the induced map on $G/\ker\theta$. (ii) $|\theta(G):\theta^2(G)|\le|G:\theta(G)|$; induct on $n$ using the restriction of $\theta$ to $\theta(G)$.
